steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Subject's body temperature, oxygen saturation levels, breathing, and heart rate are all normal.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The operation was a success.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Good work, everyone.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: It's finally over... What a miracle, right?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: This might be strange for me to say, but to be honest, I never thought this operation was going to be successful at all...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Persistence on a subjective level and the inability to give up are perhaps one and the same. If we consider solely the outcome, perhaps we should take solace we persisted through this ordeal.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Chloe is a brave girl. She never gave up on life, and as doctors, we must never give up before the patient.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Considering how high the patient's cell-Originium assimilation levels are, I really can't imagine how it feels...

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: This is all very strange, though. We've never seen such symptoms before in Oripathy, and her organs are still somewhat functional even though most of them have already completely crystallized.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: If we write a paper out of this, it will draw considerable attention in the medical science community. It could be a huge breakthrough to Oripathy medical theory.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A breakthrough, or perhaps the disease has mutated in ways beyond our comprehension. It's hard to say which.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is worth taking a closer look into. I will head to the laboratory later to analyze—

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: That's got to have broken the record for the longest procedure, hasn't it? That was, what, seventy-three hours? Seventy-five?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Seventy-nine hours and forty-five minutes.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I changed shifts twice the last couple of days, but you never left the operating room even once. And now you want to go to the lab?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Kal'tsit, you've been way too industrious ever since your trip to Victoria. Like, even more so than before.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Is there another reason to this?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In a number of ways, yes.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You were there in the meeting. You know the predicament that Rhodes Island is in right now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We only have so much time, Warfarin.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I could say the same for your stamina or sanity.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: No one can keep burning themselves out like this. Not even you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I know my own condition better than anyone, and I will take the most reasonable course of action.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I can trust you on that first part, but if your 'reasonable course of action' involves working day in and day out without end, then I have to stop you.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Your experiment won't suddenly grow legs and run away. I can help you, too, but only if you actually live to see it to fruition.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I am a doctor, too. You can't tell me to watch my coworker keep on endangering her life. What you are doing is a bad example for the entire Medical Department.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: So, get out of Medical right now, head to the canteen for a bite to eat, and go back to your own room right now. There, you can do whatever you want.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I'm locking the lab's door. Until you get eight hours of rest, don't let me see your face here.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Okay.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Save it. No amount of begging will—

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: I beg your pardon?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will follow your advice.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Thank you all for participating in this procedure. You have all earned some well-deserved rest. I, too, will stop my work for the time being.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Is there anything else?

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: N—No...

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: It kinda feels like... you've gotten more reasonable since your trip to Victoria...

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: How about I give you a thorough medical check—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your time is just as valuable as mine. Let's not squander it on such meaningless pursuits.

steps.name: Warfarin
steps.text: Hmph...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I'll leave the postoperative observation to you. If anything comes up, contact me immediately.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Thank you for all your hard work, Warfarin.

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: Amiya, we're really in a pretty tight spot right now.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I know... but we need a little more time for a solution...

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: *sigh*... To think we're always short-staffed. I wonder if there's anyone—

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: Whoa, what the f—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit?!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Amiya, you seem kind of tense.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I... I'm just a little surprised.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I don't think I've ever seen you in the canteen... so I thought maybe you...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Naturally, I need to eat for sustenance.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What about you, Amiya? Have you not had lunch yet?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Not yet... I'm helping the logistics operators to take inventory of our food supplies for the winter.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Do you want anything to eat? Today's menu is... carrot cake, carrot pie, and creamy golden carrot soup...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It sounds like there isn't much variety.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Well, about that...

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: To tell the truth, we did run into a small issue...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We have more carrots than we can eat.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: After our last stop in Rim Billiton, the mine workers that we treated there insisted on giving us carrots to show their gratitude. Lots and lots of carrots...

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: Yes... Lots of them.
Amiya turns around and points at the mountain of carrots.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There isn't much room in the kitchen, and we don't have anywhere else to put the carrots.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We don't want any of it to go to waste, so... all we can do is to use them up as fast as we can.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Perhaps we can allocate another storage room for carrots.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Huh? Are there still empty storage rooms onboard?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There was a storage used for weapons and other war essentials. It's perfect for storing logistics' supplies now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now that the war is behind us, we should spend our resources toward the betterment of our employees' lives.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If you need me to, I can ask Closure to have Engineering prioritize this matter.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In fact, we can take the carrots that can't be stored here to the storage room right now.

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: We can't ask you to—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: N—No, it's okay! Just leave it to me. I'll take care of everything.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The carrots indeed look very fresh.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This will be a particularly cold winter. Perhaps we should be thankful that we received such nutritious foods.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Yeah... I still remember how Theresa was always worried about supplies every winter.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Back then, being able to buy food from nearby villages was very good news.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But there is nothing to worry about now. Rhodes Island has a lot more operators now, and we have a lot more ways to procure food. Things won't get so bad anymore.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You're right. She put in tremendous effort to make sure all the operators had enough food to make it through each winter.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: However, important as that may be, do not forget to take care of yourself, Amiya.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Be sure to take your meals.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And don't forget that you can rely on those around you whenever you need us.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Uh... Yep!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, if you have time right now, why don't we have lunch together?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What would you like to eat? We don't have a lot of choices, but still...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...Carrot cake.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Okay!

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: Amiya... Why didn't you tell her that your limitless supply of carrots is all we have left for the winter?

steps.name: Logistics Operator
steps.text: We exhausted most of our basic supplies in Victoria, and we still haven't established a stable supply line after we got back to Rim Billiton.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit's been very busy... Let's not give her any more to worry about...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The weather forecast says the snowstorm will calm down a little in three days. We should be able to cross the valley and buy supplies at the cities to the north.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The barrenlands are dangerous. We should assign more field operators to the convoy. I'll chart the route...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Don't worry. We'll make it through the winter.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hm... If this won't do, then how 'bout this proposal? I guarantee—

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Closure.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In the past forty minutes, you've shown me twenty modification proposals for Rhodes Island's nighttime corridor lighting system.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The significant majority of them are not remotely feasible.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Well, I'm working on the right plan. I just need a little inspiration.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We needn't have a meeting over this matter. This is something you alone can decide, and you are merely wasting my time right now.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But you ended up sitting here in the Convalescent Garden for forty whole minutes! How could you call that a waste of time?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Did Warfarin ask you to come find me?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Bingo!

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: That's not the point though. What's important is that you really need some rest. That's something that everybody with eyes can tell right away.

spans.text: That's not the point though. What's important is that you
need some rest. That's something that everybody with eyes can tell right away.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Have you ever paid this place a real visit ever since it was fixed?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I know each and every facility aboard Rhodes Island well.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: No, no, no. What I'm saying is, as a normal Rhodes Island operator, you really oughta enjoy places like this where you can relax your mind.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Loosen up a bit, take a deep breath, and enjoy the feeling of being surrounded by all these living plants.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: I bet you haven't noticed all these weeds and whatnot that Lena has been planting here or what they are called.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Star Valerians. First discovered by the Gallic scholar Jacques in 817. After the Battle of the Four Emperors, it was brought to Victoria.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It was widely cultivated for its aesthetic and medicinal value, and it is the primary ingredient in many hypnotics.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Gosh darn it. I forgot you had botanist listed on your resume.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Thank you, Closure.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But if you don't need me for anything important, I shall return to the Medical Department to write my report.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Ehh, come on, can't you at least finish your tea first? Think of this as having afternoon tea with your buddy.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Just this cup of tea, then.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Tsk, always so stingy with your time...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: By the way, Kal'tsit, how long have we known each other?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Twelve years.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The year was 1086. After we excavated the Rhodes Island landship, Babel needed a sufficiently skilled engineer who can be trusted.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Theresa told me there was a self-taught genius engineer in Kazdel who was rumored to have laid one-fourth of Kazdel's nomadic cities' Originium electrical circuits all by herself.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: When Babel reached out to you, you were linking the electricity of three districts to assemble an electric hot-air balloon.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Whoa, you remember even the year? Here I thought old people tend not to fuss about when things happened in the past.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I am not that forgetful yet.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: But in these twelve years, you haven't had tea with me even once! Not once! And you call yourself a friend?!

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...I don't remember.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hmph—

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Has it really only been twelve years, though? It kinda feels like it's been a lot longer than that.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A lot has happened in these twelve years.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Mind if I ask something? Just out of curiosity?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Do twelve years go by in the blink of an eye to you?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It is not easy to measure a sense of time with a metric. All we can do is speak in terms of relativity.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Twelve years is not a particularly long stretch of time. That said, everything that happened during these twelve years is irreplaceable to me.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hmm... That's what you say, but I'm still really curious.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If everything around you goes by in the blink of an eye, do you think of everybody around you as insignificant? Like the plants in this greenhouse?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: To the significant majority of races, Vampires likewise have an unbelievably long lifespan. Do you feel that way yourself?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Well, I'm still a pretty young gal myself... Maybe I'll feel differently once I'm, god forbid, as old as Warfarin.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I do not proclaim to be a gardener over all other lives that live upon Terra. Never have I, and never will I. This has nothing to do with how long I have lived.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Even though you talk like a grumpy old gardener every time you're worried about something?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hm, maybe we should talk about something else...

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Say, when you dug Rhodes Island out of the ground, did you think about what it was going to become?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I did.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That said, what it has become is nothing like what I imagined.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: So your predictions of the future can be wrong, too?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Uh, no offense! Just blurted that out.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I've made many mistakes, Closure.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: No one can completely take control of her own future. Not even a Cyclops's Originium Arts can see all of time's possibilities.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Time is like a river. On this drifting boat, we have no way to control the flow of the water or the wind, and we cannot see the reefs and water currents underneath us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Most of the time, all we can do is hoist the sails. That alone is an exhausting enough ordeal.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Isn't that exactly the issue, though?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: If we go by your analogy, you just keep holding tight onto the sails for dear life, not even wanting to let go for a second. How could a person stay so tense for so long? If you work yourself so hard, those ropes are gonna snap.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I agree with your viewpoint.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Rhodes Island will undoubtedly face many more challenges in the future. Both Amiya and the Doctor shoulder heavy responsibilities, and we need someone to share their burden in a different way.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Closure, this is something that only you can do.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: *sigh*... You're still worried about others. Too much on your mind, and you're bound to forget what's actually in front of you right this moment.

spans.text: worried about others. Too much on your mind, and you're bound to forget what's actually in front of you right this moment.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: For example, I bet you didn't notice what was in that cup of tea while you were rambling on and on.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: What's... in this tea?

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Don't worry. It's just a herbal tea that Lena formulated. Really calms your mind, especially so for someone who hasn't had any shut-eye for three days straight.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Hmph... Finally got this old hag to get some rest.

steps.name: Closure
steps.text: Sleep well in the garden, Kal'tsit.

options: I thought my medical checkup isn't for a couple days yet?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Indeed it is, but I personally need to fully grasp your condition.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The environment of the battlefield is particularly harsh to you. I believe your health condition requires close attention.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The tools I have on hand are more than enough for me to carry out this examination. No complaints, Doctor. This will save us both a lot of time.

options: I heard Warfarin kicked you out of Medical?
She just wants you get the rest you need.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Owing to certain external factors, I've chosen to halt my work at the Medical Department today. However, that does not mean I will waste my time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Warfarin's concerns are entirely unnecessary. You should have a decent grasp of her personality already.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A lot of times, she is actually not as nonsensical as she appears on the surface. She works with the mindset of a responsible doctor, albeit an overly cautious one as a result.

options: But the fact is you have the others worried.
A doctor needs to take care of herself, too.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You needn't worry about me. I have sufficient knowledge and techniques to handle my own problems. I will not allow myself to collapse when I am needed.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I am not as weak as you think I am. To the contrary, your body requires more attention. I see that a few of your body indices are somewhat unstable.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Work-life balance, perhaps?

options: I've been working on some Originium-related research.
I want to take on some more of your burden.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Have you made progress? Or have you perhaps run into a bottleneck?

options: Perhaps I'll have a surprise for you soon.
Not being able to remember the knowledge I had before irritates me.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I am happy that you are willing to continue making such attempts.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A significant part of Rhodes Island's medical research results are built atop of your previous research. I myself am looking forward to you making further breakthroughs and bringing these lands a new turning point.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But more importantly, you are making this decision on your own will.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You need not be impatient. Although I am just as anxious to see the fruits of your labor bring a turning point to our predicament, but this is not something that can be rushed.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Your past experiences have proven you can regain your past knowledge bit by bit through effort. What we need is patience and time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You are putting in the effort toward this endeavor, and the meaning behind it has far exceeded its outcome.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: In any case, I hope that you can maintain a healthy and manageable condition.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Rhodes Island will need you even more going forward.

options: I am doing my best to work out and get ripped.
So what's your medical advice for me?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Control your work-life balance. It will be beneficial to your immune system, although I know that is very difficult for you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now do what you need. In addition to monitoring your body's condition, I will take full responsibility of your health and safety.

options: Does having a patient like me give you a headache?
I'm very fortunate to have a doctor like you.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That is not a very proper way to put it.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Dr. {@nickname}, you are a special existence, and you shoulder a special mission.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I believe in your vision, and I will assist you in this undertaking as I always have. As a mere assistant to your vision.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There is no need to thank a person merely because she carries out her duty.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I will never go against my promise, especially when I now have even more reasons to continue to defend everything.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: At the very least, you can trust me when it comes to your safety.

options: Kal'tsit, I have a question.
Why did you choose to become a doctor?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Oripathy is not the crux of all the lands' problems, but it is undoubtedly the most direct source of the hardships and sufferings that countless lives face.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It seems you don't need a special reason to choose to treat Oripathy.

options: Before you became a doctor, you had other responsibilities, didn't you?
Before you became Kal'tsit of Rhodes Island, you probably had another identity too.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is not a pervading responsibility. Instead, it's one of the many methods that I've attempted to fulfill my one and only mission.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And I only realized later, but this is also one of the countless ways that I understand this world.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I learned to not scrutinize everything on these lands purely purposefully, and because of this, I realized that these lands need to be cured of far more than just violence.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: With respect to violence, a cure would be difficult and complicated, as such a method could only be predicated upon trust.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This is a method that I never once attempted in the past, and anxious though I was, I nonetheless had to stop thinking before attempting to find the answer.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: And it was as if someone had told me... even if it ended up taking me a lot of time.

options: Was it a very long amount of time?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It was probably much longer than who you are now could ever imagine.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The metric of time is relative. The two hundred years that I spent as a doctor seem particularly long because of everything that I lost.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Now, I see possibilities I have never before seen, and I have things that I never once possessed.

options: The current Rhodes Island?
The friends we have now?
The opportunity that we have?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Certainly, they all fit the criteria, but there is far more.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I persisted and made it to this point because of my original mission, and what I gained has far exceeded what I once could comprehend.

options: For merely a 'mission'?
That has to be an important mission.
That has to be a difficult mission.
That has to be a mission you can't ever give up on.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Correct.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I may not be able to thoroughly explain to you its meaning, but one thing that I am certain of is that it is the reason why the individual 'Kal'tsit' stands here now.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: As such, no matter the reason, giving up has never been an option.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I am grateful to the person who gave me that mission.

options: I am happy you're willing to tell me all that.
I never thought I'd get the chance to have a chat with you like this.
Is this part of the medical checkup too?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: At the very least, it's predicated on trust.

options: I guess this will be a long day.
Are you smiling?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: ...A long day.
